require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe Status do
  subject { Fabricate(:status, account: alice) }

  let_it_be(:alice) { Fabricate(:account, username: 'alice') }
  let_it_be(:bob)   { Fabricate(:account, username: 'bob') }
  let_it_be(:other) { Fabricate(:status, account: bob, text: 'Skulls for the skull god! The enemy\'s gates are sideways!') }

  describe '#local?' do
    it 'returns true when no remote URI is set' do
      expect(subject.local?).to be true
    end

    it 'returns false if a remote URI is set' do
      alice.update(domain: 'example.com')
      subject.save
      expect(subject.local?).to be false
    end

    it 'returns true if a URI is set and `local` is true' do
      subject.update(uri: 'example.com', local: true)
      expect(subject.local?).to be true
    end
  end

  describe '#reblog?' do
    it 'returns true when the status reblogs another status' do
      subject.reblog = other
      expect(subject.reblog?).to be true
    end

    it 'returns false if the status is self-contained' do
      expect(subject.reblog?).to be false
    end
  end

  describe '#reply?' do
    it 'returns true if the status references another' do
      subject.thread = other
      expect(subject.reply?).to be true
    end

    it 'returns false if the status is self-contained' do
      expect(subject.reply?).to be false
    end
  end

  describe '#verb' do
    context 'when destroyed?' do
      it 'returns :delete' do
        subject.destroy!
        expect(subject.verb).to be :delete
      end
    end

    context 'when not destroyed?' do
      context 'when reblog?' do
        it 'returns :share' do
          subject.reblog = other
          expect(subject.verb).to be :share
        end
      end

      context 'when not reblog?' do
        it 'returns :post' do
          subject.reblog = nil
          expect(subject.verb).to be :post
        end
      end
    end
  end

  describe '#object_type' do
    it 'is note when the status is self-contained' do
      expect(subject.object_type).to be :note
    end

    it 'is comment when the status replies to another' do
      subject.thread = other
      expect(subject.object_type).to be :comment
    end
  end

  describe '#content' do
    it 'returns the text of the status if it is not a reblog' do
      expect(subject.content).to eql subject.text
    end

    it 'returns the text of the reblogged status' do
      subject.reblog = other
      expect(subject.content).to eql other.text
    end
  end

  describe '#target' do
    it 'returns nil if the status is self-contained' do
      expect(subject.target).to be_nil
    end

    it 'returns nil if the status is a reply' do
      subject.thread = other
      expect(subject.target).to be_nil
    end

    it 'returns the reblogged status' do
      subject.reblog = other
      expect(subject.target).to eq other
    end
  end

  describe '#reblogs_count' do
    it 'is the number of reblogs' do
      Fabricate(:status, account: bob, reblog: subject)
      Fabricate(:status, account: alice, reblog: subject)

      expect(subject.reblogs_count).to eq 2
    end

    it 'is decremented when reblog is removed' do
      reblog = Fabricate(:status, account: bob, reblog: subject)
      expect(subject.reblogs_count).to eq 1
      reblog.destroy
      expect(subject.reblogs_count).to eq 0
    end

    it 'does not fail when original is deleted before reblog' do
      reblog = Fabricate(:status, account: bob, reblog: subject)
      expect(subject.reblogs_count).to eq 1
      expect { subject.destroy }.to_not raise_error
      expect(described_class.find_by(id: reblog.id)).to be_nil
    end
  end

  describe '#untrusted_reblogs_count' do
    before do
      alice.update(domain: 'example.com')
      subject.status_stat.tap do |status_stat|
        status_stat.untrusted_reblogs_count = 0

- **Factory/DB setup dominated runtime**:
  - `spec/requests/cache_spec.rb`: 30.16s (258 read-only `GET` examples; 81% of time spent fabricating identical records per example).
  - `spec/requests/api/**`: 72.22s across 1,073 examples; 58% of time spent in `Fabricate` (`user`: 802x / 19.6s, `status`: 272x / 14.1s, `account`: 470x / 11.2s, `bookmark`: 280x / 6.3s, `admin_user`: 216x / 5.2s, `login_activity`: 2,050x / 2.8s, `accessible_access_token`: 902x / 1.6s).
  - `spec/requests/activitypub/**`: 21.25s across 108 examples; 88% of time spent in `Fabricate` (`replies_spec.rb` alone was 13.89s, creating 7 statuses per example x 45 examples; `contexts_spec.rb` fabricated `DESCENDANTS_LIMIT = 60` statuses without stubbing the constant in `GET #show`).
  - `spec/requests/signature_verification_spec.rb`: 8.47s across 30 examples, ~90% spent running `Rails.application.routes.draw` + `Rails.application.reload_routes!` per example.
- **Inline Sidekiq overhead**: Running `Sidekiq.testing!(:inline)` executed distribution, ActivityPub, notification, and mail workers unnecessarily on almost all 1,877 request examples; only 8 request spec files depended on inline Sidekiq (4 during HTTP execution, 4 only during notification/conversation test data setup).

### Optimizations Applied in Phase 2

1. **Default `Sidekiq.testing!(:fake)` for Request Specs (`spec/rails_helper.rb`)**:
   - Extended fake Sidekiq default to `%i(model request)`, tagging the 4 request contexts that test inline job side effects with `:inline_sidekiq` (`api/v1/admin/account_actions_spec.rb`, `api/v1/reports_spec.rb`, `api/v1/statuses/favourites_spec.rb`, `api/v1/timelines/home_spec.rb`) and wrapping `before_all` setup in `Sidekiq::Testing.inline!` for the 4 notification/conversation specs.
2. **Shared API Authentication & Authorization Examples (`spec/support/api_authentication.rb`, `spec/support/examples/api.rb`)**:
   - Converted `'with API authentication'` to create `default_auth_user` and `default_auth_token` once per group via `let_it_be`, updating `default_auth_token.scopes` in-transaction when `scopes` is overridden (eliminating user/token fabrication across 166 `'forbidden for wrong scope'` examples and ~700+ standard API examples).
   - Updated `'forbidden for wrong role'` (73 examples across admin API specs) to update `super()`'s `role_id` inside the rolled-back transaction instead of fabricating a new `User` + `Account` + `AccessToken` per example.
   - Migrated API request specs that manually duplicated the 4-line `user`/`scopes`/`token`/`headers` boilerplate to `include_context 'with API authentication'`.
3. **Pre-parsed Test RSA Private Key (`spec/support/signing_keys_helpers.rb`)**:
   - Parsed `PRIVATE_RSA_TEST_KEY` once into `PARSED_PRIVATE_RSA_TEST_KEY` instead of calling `OpenSSL::PKey.read` on every signed ActivityPub request.
4. **Targeted Shared Setup (`let_it_be` / `before_all`) in Top Slow Request Specs**:
   - `spec/requests/cache_spec.rb`: 30.16s -> 5.80s
   - `spec/requests/activitypub/replies_spec.rb`: 13.89s -> 2.79s
   - `spec/requests/signature_verification_spec.rb`: 8.47s -> ~0.5s (moved route drawing/reloading to `before_all`/`after(:all)`)
   - `spec/requests/api/v2/notifications_spec.rb`: 7.95s -> 1.85s
   - `spec/requests/api/v1/notifications_spec.rb`: 5.32s -> 2.18s
   - `spec/requests/activitypub/contexts_spec.rb`: 3.17s -> <0.5s (plus consistent `DESCENDANTS_LIMIT` stubbing)
   - Additional read-heavy specs (`timelines/{public,link,tag}_spec.rb`, `activitypub/{outboxes,collections}_spec.rb`, `accounts_spec.rb`, `statuses_spec.rb`, `statuses/activity_spec.rb`, `api/v1/statuses_spec.rb`, `api/v1/statuses/quotes_spec.rb`, `api/v1/accounts/statuses_spec.rb`, `api/v1/admin/{accounts,reports}_spec.rb`, `api/v2/admin/accounts_spec.rb`).

---

## Important Caveats for Future Optimization Phases

1. **Redis & `Rails.cache` Reset Per Example**:
   `spec/rails_helper.rb` runs `Rails.cache.clear` and `redis.flushdb` in `config.after`. Never rely on Redis data (e.g., `FeedManager` home timelines, `Trends::*`) or `Rails.cache` populated in `before_all` surviving past the first example. Keep PostgreSQL record creation in `before_all` and Redis population in `before`.
2. **Sidekiq Mode Inside `before_all`**:
   `TestProf::BeforeAll` forces `Sidekiq.testing!(:fake)` before `:begin`. If `before_all` calls a service (e.g., `PostStatusService`, `FavouriteService`) that creates required PostgreSQL records (`Notification`, `AccountConversation`) via Sidekiq workers, wrap that setup block in `Sidekiq::Testing.inline! { ... }`.
3. **Paperclip Disk Attachments**:
   Paperclip stores test uploads under `spec/test_files/` and only cleans them up in `after(:suite)`. Avoid sharing a single `let_it_be` record across examples that delete attachments on disk (e.g., `DELETE /api/v1/profile/avatar`) when sibling examples assert `expect(account.avatar).to exist`.
4. **Devise Virtual `password` Attribute**:
   `let_it_be` with `refind: true` reloads `User` via `User.find(id)`, where virtual `user.password` is `nil`. Specs that post `user.password` to `user_session_path` need either a fresh `Fabricate(:user)` or an explicit password string.
5. **Snowflake ID Ordering**:
   Pagination endpoints order by `id DESC` (Snowflake IDs). When converting mixed `let` / `let!` setups to `let_it_be`, preserve declaration order so `min_id` / `max_id` pagination link assertions see the same relative IDs.

---

## Plan & High-Value Targets for Next Phase: Factories (`spec/fabricators/`)

FactoryProf across the optimized `spec/requests` suite shows dramatic remaining upside inside `spec/fabricators/` (which will simultaneously speed up `models`, `requests`, `controllers`, `services`, `workers`, and `serializers`):

1. **`spec/fabricators/status_fabricator.rb` (Highest Priority)**:
   ```ruby
   after_create do |status|
     Fabricate(:bookmark, status: status)
   end
   ```
   Every single `Fabricate(:status)` unconditionally creates a `Bookmark`, which in turn fabricates a new `Account` -> `User` (BCrypt hash) -> 2 `LoginActivity` rows! In `spec/requests` alone, 331 of 340 `bookmark` fabrications (4.55s) are collateral from `Fabricate(:status)`. Removing this `after_create` hook (and explicitly creating bookmarks in any spec that actually tests bookmark presence/cascade deletion) will cut `Fabricate(:status)` time by more than half suite-wide.
2. **`spec/fabricators/user_fabricator.rb`**:
   ```ruby
   after_create do |user|
     2.times { Fabricate(:login_activity, user: user) }
   end
   ```
   Every `Fabricate(:user)` (and every local `Fabricate(:account)`) inserts 2 `LoginActivity` records. Moving this to a dedicated trait/fabricator or removing it where unused eliminates thousands of SQL `INSERT`s across the test suite. Pre-computing BCrypt's `encrypted_password` for the default `'123456789'` password (when `password` is not overridden) can also shave BCrypt CPU overhead.
3. **`spec/fabricators/account_fabricator.rb`**:
   Local `:account` always builds an associated `:user` (`user { |attrs| attrs[:domain].nil? ? Fabricate.build(:user, account: nil) : nil }`). Investigating whether `:account` always requires `:user` (or optimizing `:user` first so `:account` automatically becomes cheap) will reduce the ~14–25ms per-account cost.
4. **Attachment Fabricators (`media_attachment_fabricator.rb`, `custom_emoji_fabricator.rb`)**:
   Each `media_attachment` (~53ms) and `custom_emoji` (~46ms) runs Paperclip/libvips metadata & style processing; stubbing post-processing or using minimal 1x1 fixtures where dimensions/thumbnails are not under test can cut attachment factory cost significantly.

- **Inline Sidekiq overhead**: Running `Sidekiq.testing!(:inline)` executed distribution, ActivityPub, notification, and mail workers unnecessarily on almost all 1,877 request examples; only 8 request spec files depended on inline Sidekiq (4 during HTTP execution, 4 only during notification/conversation test data setup).

### Optimizations Applied in Phase 2

1. **Default `Sidekiq.testing!(:fake)` for Request Specs (`spec/rails_helper.rb`)**:
   - Extended fake Sidekiq default to `%i(model request)`, tagging the 4 request contexts that test inline job side effects with `:inline_sidekiq` (`api/v1/admin/account_actions_spec.rb`, `api/v1/reports_spec.rb`, `api/v1/statuses/favourites_spec.rb`, `api/v1/timelines/home_spec.rb`) and wrapping `before_all` setup in `Sidekiq::Testing.inline!` for the 4 notification/conversation specs.
2. **Shared API Authentication & Authorization Examples (`spec/support/api_authentication.rb`, `spec/support/examples/api.rb`)**:
   - Converted `'with API authentication'` to create `default_auth_user` and `default_auth_token` once per group via `let_it_be`, updating `default_auth_token.scopes` in-transaction when `scopes` is overridden (eliminating user/token fabrication across 166 `'forbidden for wrong scope'` examples and ~700+ standard API examples).
   - Updated `'forbidden for wrong role'` (73 examples across admin API specs) to update `super()`'s `role_id` inside the rolled-back transaction instead of fabricating a new `User` + `Account` + `AccessToken` per example.
   - Migrated API request specs that manually duplicated the 4-line `user`/`scopes`/`token`/`headers` boilerplate to `include_context 'with API authentication'`.
3. **Pre-parsed Test RSA Private Key (`spec/support/signing_keys_helpers.rb`)**:
   - Parsed `PRIVATE_RSA_TEST_KEY` once into `PARSED_PRIVATE_RSA_TEST_KEY` instead of calling `OpenSSL::PKey.read` on every signed ActivityPub request.
4. **Targeted Shared Setup (`let_it_be` / `before_all`) in Top Slow Request Specs**:
   - `spec/requests/cache_spec.rb`: 30.16s -> 5.80s
   - `spec/requests/activitypub/replies_spec.rb`: 13.89s -> 2.79s
   - `spec/requests/signature_verification_spec.rb`: 8.47s -> ~0.5s (moved route drawing/reloading to `before_all`/`after(:all)`)
   - `spec/requests/api/v2/notifications_spec.rb`: 7.95s -> 1.85s
   - `spec/requests/api/v1/notifications_spec.rb`: 5.32s -> 2.18s
   - `spec/requests/activitypub/contexts_spec.rb`: 3.17s -> <0.5s (plus consistent `DESCENDANTS_LIMIT` stubbing)
   - Additional read-heavy specs (`timelines/{public,link,tag}_spec.rb`, `activitypub/{outboxes,collections}_spec.rb`, `accounts_spec.rb`, `statuses_spec.rb`, `statuses/activity_spec.rb`, `api/v1/statuses_spec.rb`, `api/v1/statuses/quotes_spec.rb`, `api/v1/accounts/statuses_spec.rb`, `api/v1/admin/{accounts,reports}_spec.rb`, `api/v2/admin/accounts_spec.rb`).

---

## Phase 3 Summary (Factory Refactoring & Factory Usage in `models` + `requests`)

### FactoryProf Impact (`FPROF=1`)

| Metric | `spec/models` Before | `spec/models` After | `spec/requests` Before | `spec/requests` After |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Total `Fabricate` calls | 2,727 | **1,984 (-27.2%)** | 3,322 | **2,058 (-38.0%)** |
| Total `Fabricate` time | 34.47s | **18.19s (-47.2%)** | 31.01s | **13.89s (-55.2%)** |
| `status` time | 11.83s (28.1ms/call) | **3.30s (8.8ms/call)** | 9.10s (27.5ms/call) | **2.62s (7.9ms/call)** |
| `bookmark` calls / time | 424x / 6.57s | **4x / 0.04s** | 340x / 5.08s | **9x / 0.10s** |
| `account` time | 8.55s (13.0ms/call) | **5.44s (8.9ms/call)** | 7.30s (14.3ms/call) | **3.62s (8.2ms/call)** |
| `user` time | 1.80s (19.4ms/call) | **0.87s (9.6ms/call)** | 5.16s (17.2ms/call) | **2.62s (9.0ms/call)** |
| `login_activity` calls / time | 220x / 0.32s | **0x / 0.00s** | 782x / 0.89s | **0x / 0.00s** |
| `media_attachment` time | 5.35s | **4.24s** | 2.03s | **0.83s** |

### Optimizations Applied in Phase 3

1. **Eliminated Collateral `after_create` Associations (`status_fabricator.rb`, `user_fabricator.rb`)**:
   - Removed `after_create { |status| Fabricate(:bookmark, status: status) }` from `status_fabricator.rb` (previously every status created a `Bookmark` + `Account` + `Keypair` + `User`, accounting for >50% of `Fabricate(:status)` runtime).
   - Removed `after_create { |user| 2.times { Fabricate(:login_activity, user: user) } }` from `user_fabricator.rb` (eliminated ~1,000 unnecessary `LoginActivity` inserts + `Faker` calls across `models` and `requests`).
2. **Pre-computed Default BCrypt Password & Deterministic Sequences (`user_fabricator.rb`, `account_fabricator.rb`, etc.)**:
   - Pre-computed `DEFAULT_FABRICATED_USER_ENCRYPTED_PASSWORD` once at load time and assigned `@password` + `encrypted_password` in `after_build` when `:password` is not overridden, preserving Devise's virtual `user.password` attribute and `valid_password?` behavior while eliminating ~1.2ms of BCrypt hashing on every local `Account` and `User` build/create.
   - Replaced `Faker::Internet` / `Faker::Lorem` calls in high-frequency fabricators (`account`, `user`, `tag`, `preview_card`, `canonical_email_block`, `domain_block`, `email_domain_block`, `announcement`) with deterministic `sequence` values (also preventing >30-char Faker username validation flakes and non-unique `PreviewCard#url` collisions).
   - Note: Local `Account` intentionally retains `user` (`Account.without_unapproved` / `searchable` / `discoverable` require an approved, confirmed `User`).
3. **Deduplicated Redundant `Account` Creation in Composite Fabricators**:
   - Updated `media_attachment`, `poll`, `status_trend`, `notification_request`, and `account_conversation` fabricators to reuse their parent record's `account` (`status.account`, `from_account`, etc.) instead of fabricating a separate `Account` + `User` + `Keypair`.
   - Removed unused default `reference_account { Fabricate.build(:account) }` from `canonical_email_block_fabricator.rb` (`reference_account` is optional; specs that test it pass it explicitly).
4. **Lightweight Default Attachment Assets (`spec/fabricators/assets/{attachment.jpg,emoji.png}`)**:
   - Added tiny 8x8 JPEG (803B) and PNG (282B) fabricator assets for `media_attachment`, `preview_card`, and `custom_emoji` defaults instead of 60KB `600x400` `attachment.jpg` and 29KB `emojo.png`, cutting Vips thumbnail + Ruby blurhash processing time by 2–3x while keeping real files on disk.
5. **Factory Usage Cleanup in `spec/models` & `spec/requests`**:
   - Avoided animated `avatar.gif` (`ffmpeg` subprocess) where static files suffice (`media_attachment_spec.rb` `#needs_redownload?`, `api/v1/profiles_spec.rb` shared setup).
   - Replaced `Fabricate.build` with `described_class.new` for pure attribute unit tests (`expireable.rb` `#expires_in=`, `media_attachment_spec.rb` `#to_param`).
   - Converted remaining repeated factory setups in `status_spec.rb`, `account_spec.rb`, `user_spec.rb`, `media_attachment_spec.rb`, `media_spec.rb`, `api/v1/media_spec.rb`, `api/v1/profiles_spec.rb`, `api/v2/search_spec.rb`, `api/v1/directories_spec.rb`, `api/v1/collections_spec.rb`, `api/v1/accounts/{follower,following}_accounts_spec.rb`, and `spec/requests/admin/**` (`admin_user` sign-in) to `let_it_be` / `before_all`.

---

## Important Caveats for Future Optimization Phases

1. **Redis & `Rails.cache` Reset Per Example**:
   `spec/rails_helper.rb` runs `Rails.cache.clear` and `redis.flushdb` in `config.after`. Never rely on Redis data (e.g., `FeedManager` home timelines, `Trends::*`) or `Rails.cache` populated in `before_all` surviving past the first example. Keep PostgreSQL record creation in `before_all` and Redis population in `before`.
2. **Sidekiq Mode Inside `before_all`**:
   `TestProf::BeforeAll` forces `Sidekiq.testing!(:fake)` before `:begin`. If `before_all` calls a service (e.g., `PostStatusService`, `FavouriteService`) that creates required PostgreSQL records (`Notification`, `AccountConversation`) via Sidekiq workers, wrap that setup block in `Sidekiq::Testing.inline! { ... }`.
3. **Paperclip Disk Attachments**:
   Paperclip stores test uploads under `spec/test_files/` and only cleans them up in `after(:suite)`. Avoid sharing a single `let_it_be` record across examples that delete attachments on disk (e.g., `DELETE /api/v1/profile/avatar`, `DELETE /api/v1/media/:id`) when sibling examples assert attachment existence.
4. **Devise Virtual `password` Attribute**:
   `let_it_be` with `refind: true` reloads `User` via `User.find(id)`, where virtual `user.password` is `nil`. Specs that post `user.password` to `user_session_path` need either a fresh `Fabricate(:user)` or an explicit password string.
5. **Snowflake ID Ordering**:
   Pagination endpoints order by `id DESC` (Snowflake IDs). When converting mixed `let` / `let!` setups to `let_it_be`, preserve declaration order so `min_id` / `max_id` pagination link assertions see the same relative IDs.

---

## Plan & High-Value Targets for Future Optimization Phases (`controllers`, `services`, `workers`, `serializers`, `views`)

- All suites (`controllers`, `services`, `workers`, `serializers`, `presenters`, `policies`) automatically benefit from the Phase 3 `spec/fabricators/` optimizations (`status`, `user`, `account`, `media_attachment`, `preview_card`, `poll`, etc.).

- **Sidekiq Default Mode for `controllers`, `serializers`, `presenters`, `policies`, `views`**: Extending `Sidekiq.testing!(:fake)` in `spec/rails_helper.rb` beyond `%i(model request)` (with `:inline_sidekiq` opt-in where needed) and applying `let_it_be` / `before_all` to slow `controllers` and `services` specs are the top high-leverage next steps.

messages.content:
We have profiled and optimized factory definitions (`spec/fabricators/`) and factory usage across `spec/models` and `spec/requests`, reducing their combined runtime by **34.6%** relative to Phase 2 (**4.55x faster** than the initial baseline) with zero test failures and no application code changes.

### Summary of Findings & Optimizations

1. **Eliminated Collateral `after_create` Associations (`status_fabricator.rb`, `user_fabricator.rb`)**:
   - Removed `after_create { |status| Fabricate(:bookmark, status: status) }` from `spec/fabricators/status_fabricator.rb`, which previously created an unrequested `Bookmark` + `Account` + `Keypair` + `User` on every status fabrication (>50% of `Fabricate(:status)` runtime).
   - Removed `after_create { |user| 2.times { Fabricate(:login_activity, user: user) } }` from `spec/fabricators/user_fabricator.rb`, eliminating ~1,000 unnecessary `LoginActivity` inserts across `models` and `requests`.

2. **Pre-computed Default BCrypt Hash & Deterministic Sequences (`user_fabricator.rb`, `account_fabricator.rb`, etc.)**:
   - Pre-computed `DEFAULT_FABRICATED_USER_ENCRYPTED_PASSWORD` once at load time and assigned `@password` + `encrypted_password` in `after_build` when `:password` is not overridden, avoiding per-record BCrypt hashing while preserving Devise's virtual `password` attribute and validation semantics.
   - Replaced `Faker` calls in high-frequency fabricators (`account`, `user`, `tag`, `preview_card`, `canonical_email_block`, `domain_block`, `email_domain_block`, `announcement`) with fast deterministic sequences/strings.

3. **Deduplicated Redundant `Account` Creation & Lightweight Attachment Assets**:
   - Updated `media_attachment`, `poll`, `status_trend`, `notification_request`, and `account_conversation` fabricators to reuse their parent record's `account` by default instead of fabricating duplicate `Account` + `User` + `Keypair` graphs, and removed the unused default `reference_account` from `canonical_email_block`.
   - Added tiny 8x8 JPEG/PNG default assets in `spec/fabricators/assets/` (`attachment.jpg`, `emoji.png`) for `media_attachment`, `preview_card`, and `custom_emoji`, cutting Vips thumbnail and Ruby blurhash overhead by 2–3x.

4. **Shared Setup & Factory Usage in `spec/models` and `spec/requests`**:
   - Replaced `Fabricate.build` with `described_class.new` in pure attribute specs (`expireable.rb` `#expires_in=`, `media_attachment_spec.rb` `#to_param`) and avoided animated GIF `ffmpeg` transcoding where static fixtures suffice (`media_attachment_spec.rb`, `api/v1/profiles_spec.rb`).
   - Converted repeated factory setups in `status_spec.rb`, `account_spec.rb`, `user_spec.rb`, `media_attachment_spec.rb`, `media_spec.rb`, `api/v1/media_spec.rb`, `api/v1/profiles_spec.rb`, `api/v2/search_spec.rb`, `api/v1/directories_spec.rb`, `api/v1/collections_spec.rb`, `api/v1/accounts/{follower,following}_accounts_spec.rb`, and `spec/requests/admin/**` (`admin_user`) to `let_it_be` / `before_all`.

### Benchmark Results (`~js ~search ~streaming`, Single Process)

| Suite | Examples | Baseline | After Phase 2 | After Phase 3 (Factories) | Improvement vs Phase 2 | Total Speedup vs Baseline |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `spec/models` | 1,795 | 129.7s | 35.5s | **23.4s** | **-34.1%** | **5.54x faster (-82.0%)** |
| `spec/requests` | 1,877 | 172.1s | 65.9s | **42.9s** | **-34.9%** | **4.01x faster (-75.1%)** |
| **Combined** | **3,672** | **301.8s** | **101.4s** | **66.3s** | **-34.6%** | **4.55x faster (-78.0%)** |

Detailed FactoryProf metrics, caveats, and plans for future optimization phases have been recorded in `docs/RSPEC_OPTIMIZATION.md`.
